expected: The same over-budget request sent twice must be denied OVER_BUDGET both times with byte-identical per-capability byte attribution (I6: deterministic compilation under failure), and never mint or coalesce to a wildcard.
observed: Both identical requests returned status=denied, denial_code=OVER_BUDGET, with a 266-byte detail string that was byte-for-byte identical across the two calls; the entire response object was identical except for the per-request grant_id ULID (expected). Detail: 'policy is 2958 chars, budget 1748, over by 1210; s3.read-prefix: 1460 chars, over by 1210; s3.write-prefix: 1456 chars, over by 1210' (repeated). No wildcard was emitted (the broker denied instead of coalescing, honoring I2), and the audit record for the denied grant carried outcome=denied with no access_key_id, no session_token/secret, and no minted_at, proving no STS mint occurred. A single s3.read-prefix (512-char prefix) compiles to 1548 chars (calibration mint, released); combining it with a distinct s3.write-prefix (512-char prefix) pushes the policy to 2958 chars, over the 1748 budget. The budget denial fires before approval parking even though s3.write-prefix requires_approval.
